title: Viability of electroweak baryogenesis
bottleneck: Electroweak baryogenesis would generate the matter asymmetry at the weak scale where it is testable, but it requires a strongly first-order electroweak phase transition and new CP violation, both increasingly constrained by Higgs coupling measurements and the null electron electric dipole moment searches. The minimal Standard Model transition is a smooth crossover, not first-order.
why_it_blocks: This was the only baryogenesis scenario testable at colliders; its near-exclusion removes the most experimentally accessible explanation of our matter-dominated universe.
current_state: Extended Higgs sectors can still rescue a first-order transition, keeping the scenario alive in narrow parameter regions that future colliders and EDM experiments will probe decisively. The null electron electric dipole moment results constrain new CP-violating phases so tightly that only narrow corners of extended Higgs sectors survive.
